questions.knowledge_point: The Vertical Asymptote of a Transformed Logarithmic Function
questions.problem: Find the equation of the vertical asymptote of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)+1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the vertical asymptote of the function $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ is $x=0.$

To find the equation of the vertical asymptote of $f(x)$, we set the argument of the logarithmic term equal to zero, and solve for $x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =0 \\ x & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=3.$

questions.knowledge_point: The Range of a Transformed Logarithmic Function
questions.worked_solution:
The range of the function $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ is $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

Horizontal and vertical shifts and stretches do not affect the range of a logarithmic function.

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ and the function has no maximum value.

questions.knowledge_point: The Vertical Asymptote of a Transformed Logarithmic Function
questions.problem: Find the equation of the vertical asymptote of the function $f(x)=2{log}_{4}⁡(-3x)+6.$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the vertical asymptote of the function $y={log}_{4}⁡x$ is $x=0.$

To find the equation of the vertical asymptote of $f(x),$ we set the argument of the logarithmic term equal to zero, and solve for $x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x & =0 \\ x & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=0.$

questions.knowledge_point: The Root of a Transformed Logarithmic Function
questions.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x)$, we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
{log}_{2}⁡(4-2x)+1=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{2}⁡(4-2x)+1 & =0 \\ {log}_{2}⁡(4-2x) & =-1 \\ {2}^{{log}_{2}⁡(4-2x)} & ={2}^{-1} \\ 4-2x & =\frac{1}{2} \\ -2x & =-\frac{7}{2} \\ x & =\frac{7}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=\frac{7}{4}.$
